summary: Round 9 recheck, 26 Sep ~13:00-13:40 UTC. It picks three closed or deferred ideas that rounds 2-8 did not re-check. Already covered and skipped: floatout, I-077/78, tempfuse, swapfix, clip-boundary, axis-flip, head-shift scale, refined-dup collapse, leaf prune, frozen-frame, already-divided, AdaBN, stitch, efpost, linefit, gap LAP/sandwich, zsplit, headroom, z-shift, DivNet veto, split-flow relink, forkblob/sister floor, DNVETO, ANTIPAR and the insertion cap/re-tune. Two of the three were measured on CPU on the exp60 x138 lab (56 clips, official metric; the control reproduces div TP/FP/FN 16/25/83). None revives, and the plan does not change: finals #37 + #38, no OK request, nothing submitted, pushed or committed. (A) I-276, 'mimic GT division annotation noise' (forks shifted in time or space to match GT errors). Round 8 deferred it untested. It is now CLOSED by measurement. The official metric already tolerates +-1 frame. Of the 83 FN GT divisions, 31 have no predicted fork within +-4 frames and 46 have their nearest fork 12 um or more away. Only 1 FN (44b6_eb2880fc: a fork 2 frames late at 2.1 um, labelled FP) could be reached by a timing shift. No GT-free rule can move that one fork without moving the 16 TP forks. (B) The link-stage LB family: relink OFF, learned bonus 2.5, gshift and association variants (I-177/179/180/181). STAYS CLOSED, and the closure is now stronger. The old reading was 'ties at the noise floor'. With the curator's correction that our kernels are deterministic, probes 21/22/23 (all 0.945 vs 0.947) are three real -0.002 public reads. On x138, the neighbourhood-flow prior (12 neighbours within 40 um, gated) generalises a global shift, and the readmit runs inside the relink, so relink OFF is not a one-stage change. (C) I-222, x138's retention guard (per-frame fallback to primary-only candidates). STAYS CLOSED, with a new fact. The fallback depends on the embryo: 44b6 falls back on 33% of frames (47% weighted by edges; 2 clips at 100%), 6bba on 4% (26 of 39 clips at 0). No clip-level harm shows: 44b6 edge J is 0.882 with >= 20% fallback vs 0.877 without. So on hidden embryos x138 and both finals run a different detector mix per embryo. The mix is shared by #37 and #38, so it needs no finals action. Testing the counterfactual needs a GPU, so it goes to the post-deadline list.

findings.what: I-276, 'mimic GT division annotation noise': shape forks to match systematic GT division errors (split at the wrong coordinates; daughter one frame later). Source: a forum comment. OLD VERDICT (round 8, research/wf_ideas_v4/round8/scan_browser.json): deferred-after-deadline WITHOUT any measurement ('new code past R8'). WHAT CHANGED: the exp60 x138 lab can label every fork officially and locate every FN GT division, so the reach can be measured instead of assumed. MEASURED (56 clips; control = x138 final graphs, div TP/FP/FN 16/25/83 = the lab's number; ins35 = #35-config insertion, 25/31/74): (1) The metric already absorbs +-1 frame. In tools/official/src/tracking_cellmot/division_metrics.py, the parent side is the GT divider plus its predecessor, the fork may be the matched parent or its successor, and the daughter side is the child plus its grandchildren. (2) FN GT divisions: 31/83 have no predicted fork within +-4 frames, 46/83 have their nearest fork >= 12 um away, 5 have it at 7-12 um with |dt| 0-4 (the only |dt| <= 1 case is 6bba_2312ac41, whose 11.8 um fork is not labelled FP, so it is not available), and 1 has it at < 7 um (44b6_eb2880fc: fork 2 frames after the GT divider, 2.1 um, labelled FP). (3) FP forks: 15/25 have no GT divider within +-4 frames, and only 1 (the same eb2880fc fork) is within 7 um. ins35 has the same shape (20/74 none, 1 at < 7 um). NEW VERDICT: CLOSED by measurement, and removed from the post-deadline list as a mechanism. At most 1 of 83 FN and 1 of 25 FP are timing- or position-shiftable. No GT-free rule can pick that fork without moving the 16 TP forks. The division loss is missing forks (detection or linking), as the round-8 reach audit found.

findings.what: Link-stage LB family: I-177 motion relink OFF (probe 21 exp40), I-179 learned bonus 1.0 -> 2.5 (probe 22 exp41), I-180 per-frame global-shift correction 'gshift' (probe 23 exp42), I-181 association-rule variants (takaito/haideptry mutual-best / relative-rank beta; probe 24 verbatim 0.944). OLD VERDICT (CONTEXT l.1203-1217, 22-24 Sep): 'all three -0.002 vs exp29 = ties at the noise floor, slightly negative; the relink stage of exp29 is at its local optimum'. Friend B's local +0.0053 for relink OFF was one division event, and it repaired the 44b6_87bba6c4 dense collapse. WHAT CHANGED: (1) The curator correction (CONTEXT, 25 Sep 19:05 UTC) says the '+-0.003 LB noise' does not apply to our deterministic kernels, so a 0.001 public step is real. Probes 21/22/23 are therefore three REAL -0.002 public reads, not ties. (2) The base is now x138 (experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim cell 0). Its relink is a neighbourhood-flow prior (FLOW_MODE seed, K 12, RADIUS 40 um, FLOW_GATE 1, FLOW_TIGHT 7.0 um, TIGHT 5.5, LEARNED_BONUS set to 1.0 over the code default 0.75), and the readmit (RADIUS 4 um, MIN_SCORE 0.965) and gapfill chain runs inside or after it. There are 0 'gshift' hits. A per-neighbourhood flow from 12 nearest neighbours is a strict generalisation of one per-frame global shift. (3) exp60 has no pre-relink hook, so there is no CPU replay of any relink arm (round 5). NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED, and the closure is stronger. gshift is subsumed by the flow prior. Relink OFF on x138 is no longer a one-stage change, because it removes the readmit/flow chain that x138's +0.006 rests on. The bonus change is a knob (no public ladders). All of them are edge-set changers with no honest lab bed, and R8 applies.

findings.what: I-222: x138's dual-seed retention guard. Per frame, if the blended candidates keep < 90% of the primary's, x138 falls back to primary-only candidates (fallback_scope individual_frame). OLD VERDICT (round 3, R3S-5): 'closed, not proposed'. The flicker penalty was absent (switch pairs 6.05% GT-edge FN, between blended 3.17% and primary 10.71%), the change would alter the node set (R4), and it needs a GPU lab. WHAT CHANGED: the public-vs-private split (public ~ one embryo, private ~71% other embryos) makes an embryo-dependent mode switch a shake-up factor. The 3.4x FN ratio of primary-only frames also suggested that the fallback itself could hurt. MEASURED from the exp60 guard logs (5,600 frame rows, 56 clips): primary-only fallback covers 33.1% of 44b6 frames (47% weighted by edge count; 6/17 clips >= 50%; 44b6_9be80b04 and 44b6_e28840c6 at 100%) against 3.9% of 6bba frames (4.5% weighted; 26/39 clips at 0; 6bba_ab78413d at 93%). Clip-level harm does not show. 44b6 edge J is 0.8821 on clips with >= 20% fallback (n=8) vs 0.8765 below (n=9). Spearman(fallback share, edge FN rate) is +0.16 on 44b6 and +0.05 on 6bba. The 10.71% frame FN is selection (hard frames trigger the fallback), not a measured cost. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED. NEW FACT: on hidden embryos, x138 and both finals (#37 and #38 share it) run an embryo-dependent detector mix, from almost always blended (6bba-like) to about half primary-only (44b6-like). Because both finals share it, it cannot separate them and needs no finals action. The counterfactual (blended on fallback frames) needs a GPU rerun and changes nodes, so it goes to the post-deadline list.

findings.what: x138 lab division-loss anatomy (control; ins35 in brackets): of 83 [74] FN GT divisions, 31 [20] have NO predicted fork within +-4 frames and 46 have the nearest fork >= 12 um away. Of 25 [31] FP forks, 15 [19] have no GT divider within +-4 frames, i.e. they are forks on annotated non-dividing tracks, not near-misses. The insertion removes 11 'no fork' FN (31 -> 20) and adds 4 isolated FP (15 -> 19). The division term is limited by missing forks and isolated false forks, not by timing or position offsets.
